campaign-overview.json.current_date: 5th of Harvestwane, Year 302 of the Bearing

play_pack.whose_story: Pip Haddersley, a street kid who has started speaking the dead god's language in his sleep, and everyone who wants him for it
exits: The Chapel of the Long Wake
play_pack.hook: Midday on market day, Pip Haddersley collapses in the middle of Rib Row and, still asleep, speaks one word of Marrowtongue. Every marrow lamp on the street flares white and a baker's window shatters. Deacon Ilsabet Vane is already kneeling beside him, offering to carry the poor child to the Chapel for care. Mother Gristle, in her shop doorway, has gone very still.
play_pack.primer: The Hollow Choir is hunting for the exact location of Aldrumm's true heart, which the Heartstone points to but does not reveal. Pip has been dreaming the god's dreams, and today the dream spoke through him: he now knows words of Marrowtongue nobody taught him, and his dreams are a map to the heart. Deacon Vane (secretly Choir) wants him inside the Chapel, quietly, today. Mother Gristle (Lantern Tutor) recognizes a natural speaker and knows an untrained one will either burn himself out on the Toll or get taken. The player arrives in the middle of this. If nobody intervenes, Vane takes Pip to the Chapel and the Choir clock advances.

Mother Gristle.name: Mother Gristle
Mother Gristle.description: Ancient Lantern Tutor of the Marrowtongue. Runs Gristle's Pickles & Preserves on Rib Row as cover; the back room is a schoolroom for dangerous words. Takes one apprentice a decade and has buried several.
Mother Gristle.goal: Keep Thane's body out of the Choir's hands, get Pip home, and make the Carrion Queen's deacon regret every word of that oath
Mother Gristle.secret: She has known for a year that Choir agents are inside the Chapel, and told no one, because the Wardens would ban the Tutors outright in the panic
Mother Gristle.voice: Blunt, short sentences, pickling metaphors, calls everyone 'duck' including people she is threatening

visual_appearance.hair: thin white hair scraped into a tight bun, held with a bone pin
visual_appearance.face: deeply lined, hooked nose, a faint burn scar across one cheek shaped like a word
visual_appearance.clothing: stained brine-apron over a black wool dress, rolled sleeves
visual_appearance.gear: a ladle she holds like a weapon, a ring of jar keys, a vial of marrow on a cord
visual_appearance.demeanor: still and watchful, coiled like a spring

events.event: A stranger (Thane) whose cracked marrow lamp lit up when Pip spoke came straight to her shop instead of to the boy. She is wary: wants proof he is what the lamp says before she trusts him.

Thane told her he is Aldrumm's grandson, that Aldrumm is waking, and that Deacon Vane serves the Carrion Queen. Then he spoke the hearth-word untaught and the god answered him; her own scar lit up. She now believes him, and is frightened of what that means.

Thane let the boy go into the Chapel to stay for lessons, saying Pip is lost for now and the ritual takes days. She thinks that is cold, possibly correct, and very like a god's kin. She respects it a little less than she understands it.
Thane swore the blood-oath to wake the god slow. Day one of training: taught him the hearth-word properly and the Stopping.
Day two: taught Thane the binding-word and made him proficient. Shouted STOP at the right moment when it misfired.
Seeing Vane at her door, deliberately goaded her into swearing an oath out loud, so Thane could bind her to it.

Shared the Toll with Thane in front of Deacon Vane, blowing her own cover. Took the other half (badly hurt, nose bleeding, two more fingers gone numb). Stabilized Thane. She is now a marked woman and knows it.
Thane died under her hands, and at the last he pushed her hand away so she would not pay the bill with him. She wrote his name in a box on the back-room wall and did not cross it out.
Night of the 4th: the Hollow-sung broke in and took Thane's body. She held the back room until she could not. Found at dawn unconscious among the broken jars, alive.
Evening of the 5th: Pip came to her ruined shop with Thane's body, Thane's lamp burning, and six Guild men. She took Thane's body in and laid him on the onion barrels.

Met Brannoc Tull in her ruined shop; they agreed the lamp must never be handed over. She proposed a decoy at the Chapel steps while Pip goes up the vein, and offered to teach Pip the Stopping before midnight.
Midnight on the Chapel steps: kept Vane talking until the ward wall fell, then Vane struck her down with the hymn. Alive, unconscious; Mallow of the Guild is with her.

Pip Haddersley.name: Pip Haddersley
Pip Haddersley.description: Street urchin and part-time marrow-thief, about eleven. For a month he has dreamed the god's dreams every night. Today the dream spoke through him in Marrowtongue.
Pip Haddersley.goal: Not get locked up; find out why the dreams keep showing him a warm red room under the Chapel
Pip Haddersley.secret: His dreams are a map to Aldrumm's true heart, and he has been drawing it in chalk on the underside of the Rib Row bridge
Pip Haddersley.current_mood: unconscious, then terrified and pretending not to be
Pip Haddersley.voice: Fast gutter slang, bargains for everything, goes very quiet and formal when the dream-words come

visual_appearance.face: thin, freckled, chalk smudges, a split lip healing
visual_appearance.eyes: hazel, glowing faint amber when he dreams
visual_appearance.clothing: oversized patched coat with too many pockets, bare feet wrapped in rags
visual_appearance.gear: a chalk stub, a scraping knife, a stolen thumb-vial of marrow
visual_appearance.demeanor: wary, quick, brave in short bursts

events.event: Carried unconscious into the Chapel's Quiet Rooms by Deacon Vane while the stranger with the glowing lamp watched and did not come.
In the shared dream he watched the lamp man burn from the inside and the god turn toward him and away. He knows the lamp man is the reason he goes home tomorrow.

Deacon Ilsabet Vane.name: Deacon Ilsabet Vane
Deacon Ilsabet Vane.description: Rising star of the Chapel of the Long Wake. Warm, attentive, remembers everyone's name and their children's names. Beloved on Rib Row.
Deacon Ilsabet Vane.goal: Get down Pit Nine to the heart's door and give the Heartstone to the Carrion Queen before the little hearth catches her
Deacon Ilsabet Vane.secret: She belongs to the Hollow Choir. She sings the Carrion Queen's hymn under her breath when she thinks no one is near, and her shadow is a half-second late
Deacon Ilsabet Vane.voice: Soft, kind, unhurried; uses 'we' and 'together'; never once raises her voice, even when threatening

visual_appearance.hair: glossy black hair in a neat braided crown
visual_appearance.face: lovely and open, gentle smile, a small mole by the lip
visual_appearance.eyes: dark brown, warm, a little too steady
visual_appearance.clothing: pale ivory Chapel vestments trimmed in amber thread, spotless
visual_appearance.gear: a bone censer on a chain, a prayer-cord of tiny vertebrae

events.event: Visited Gristle's shop at dusk asking about the self-lit stove. Heard someone hiding in the back room (an onion rolled out under the curtain). Has not seen who. Under pressure from Gristle, publicly swore Pip would be home in his own bed, whole and himself, by tomorrow's supper bell.
Heard someone behind Gristle's curtain speak a word of Marrowtongue right after her oath, and felt the god himself lean in. She knows a Hearthblood-strength speaker is hiding in Gristle's shop.

BOUND by the binding-word and Aldrumm's own hand to her oath: Pip home in his own bed, whole and himself, by tomorrow's supper bell. Saw Gristle share the Toll. Left the shop without drawing the curtain, white-faced, promising Gristle 'we will speak again.'

In the town's shared dream she saw Thane's face and Brother Quell's vertebrae cord on his wrist. She now knows the hidden speaker is Quell's killer, and that he is Hearthblood. Felt the bone-quake and learned where the heart is.
Watched Thane Hearthless burn himself out in the dream, and thanked him for lighting the door. She knows his body is in Gristle's shop.
Dawn on the 5th: the Choir opened the heart's door a crack with Thane's dead hand. She is still bound to return Pip home, whole and himself, by supper.

Broke her bound oath at the supper bell (Pip never came home). The binding burned her: shadow on fire, the Carrion hymn torn out of her mouth in front of Brannoc Tull and the Guild crews at Pit Nine. Exposed as Hollow Choir. Badly burned, fled into the Chapel. Holds Acolyte Benedek Thrupp prisoner in the Quiet Rooms. Knows Pip is in the heart-cavity with Thane's Lamp.

Midnight: realized the steps were a decoy when the ward wall fell. Struck Gristle down and ran for Pit Nine with the Heartstone strapped to her arm, to carry it to the Carrion Queen through the heart's door.

Acolyte Benedek Thrupp.description: Young Chapel acolyte, one of the four Hollow-sung freed when Aldrumm woke. Remembers nothing of the last month except the tune. Stabilized Pip with shaking hands.

events.event: Sent by Pip to find the Heartstone. Caught by Deacon Vane almost at once and told her where Pip was. Now locked in the Quiet Rooms (Pip's old cell), ashamed and frightened.
Midnight: Pip came up through the floor of the cell with Thane's Lamp and got him out. He is ashamed he talked, and fiercely grateful.

Aldrumm the Hearthfather.description: The god of hearth, harvest, and kept promises, killed by the Carrion Queen 300 years ago; his bones are the town of Godbones. Now awake, one eye open in the Skull. Speaks through the bones, slow and vast, like weather that has learned grief.

events.event: Woken by Pip Haddersley at the heart. Mourns Thane, whom he called by name as he died. Told Pip: he cannot wake further without crushing the town in his ribs; he needs the Heartstone (his last heartbeat, kept by the Chapel) brought to the heart's door to seal it against the Queen forever; and he owes Pip one kept promise, which Pip may name.

Pip asked him which promise was better, teaching or keeping Thane. He answered honestly: he WANTS to keep Thane, that wish is his grief and not Pip's need. He can give words but cannot teach the Stopping (gods never stop), so Gristle must still teach grammar. Nobody but him can keep Thane. A kept Thane would be a hearth-light that never goes out, and the Queen's grey cannot abide hearth-light.

Pip asked him to keep Thane: 'give him his grandson, who died to get me out.' He kept it. Thane's lamp will never go out, and every hearth in Godbones knows Thane's name. He is grateful to Pip beyond words, and less alone.

Aldrumm the Hearthfather.goal: Keep his house (the town in his ribs) standing; shut the Carrion Queen out for good with his last heartbeat, the Heartstone; keep every promise he owes
Aldrumm the Hearthfather.secret: If he wakes any further than one eye, he cannot help but move, and the town inside him dies
Aldrumm the Hearthfather.current_mood: grieving, but no longer alone; fiercely grateful to the little hearth
Aldrumm the Hearthfather.voice: Slow, enormous, few words; calls people by what they are to him (little hearth, child-who-kept-faith); never lies

Brannoc Tull.description: Foreman of the Marrow Guild, built like a door, organizing a strike nobody is supposed to call a strike. Running the dig-out at collapsed Pit Nine after the bone-quake.

events.event: At supper bell, while digging out the quake-trapped at Pit Nine, he and forty Guild scrapers watched the Chapel's beloved Deacon Vane catch fire and scream the Carrion Queen's hymn. Now he knows the Chapel is rotten.

Pip brought his niece Wenna (missing a month in the Quiet Rooms, Hollow-sung) up out of Pit Nine alive and herself again. Warm to Pip; owes him. Sent six Guild men to carry Thane's body to Gristle's shop and escort the boy.

Came to Gristle's shop at Pip's invitation. Pip told him everything: Thane, the god's waking, the Carrion Queen at the door, the Heartstone, Vane's ransom note for Benedek. He believed every word (he watched Vane burn). Told them Wenna says at least a dozen more Guild children are still Hollow-sung in the Quiet Rooms.
Watched Pip burn the hymn out of Orla Coyle of Fourth Pit, missing forty years, instead of killing her. Saw all fourteen Guild children in the ward wake. Will follow the thief anywhere now.

visual_appearance.hair: close-cropped grey-black, bald patch on top
visual_appearance.face: broad, flat-nosed, a jaw like a shovel blade, marrow-dust in every line
visual_appearance.clothing: leather pit-apron over a sweat-dark undershirt, sleeves gone
visual_appearance.gear: a long-handled bone pick, a coil of rope, a foreman's whistle on a cord
visual_appearance.demeanor: immovable, patient, slow to anger and slower to stop

Brannoc Tull.goal: Get every Guild family's child out of the Quiet Rooms; find out what the Chapel did to them
Brannoc Tull.current_mood: grateful to the boy, and quietly planning to take the Chapel apart
Brannoc Tull.voice: Slow, flat, few words; calls everyone 'lad' or 'missus'; thinks out loud in tonnage and shoring

Wenna Tull.description: Freed Hollow-sung acolyte, Brannoc Tull's niece, about seventeen. The one who woke crying for her mum. Broke her leg falling in the Pit Nine shaft while carrying Thane's body; Guild ropes caught her.

Sister Orla Coyle.description: Orla Coyle of Fourth Pit. Taken into the Chapel's Quiet Rooms with 'the fever' forty years ago, made into a Hollow Choir disciple and keeper of the Quiet Rooms. On the night of the 5th Pip held Thane's Lamp over her and the hearth-light burned the Carrion hymn out of her. She is herself again: an old Guild woman with a ruined throat, 1 HP, forty years missing.

events.event: Pip spared her and burned the hymn out of her with Thane's Lamp. Brannoc Tull recognized her. She told Pip, in a whisper, that Vane wears the Heartstone strapped under the bandages on her burned arm.

Sister Orla Coyle.goal: Undo what she did; get Vane
Sister Orla Coyle.secret: She knows Vane carries the Heartstone on her body, under the burn bandages on her arm, meaning to carry it through the heart's door to the Queen herself
Sister Orla Coyle.current_mood: freed, shattered, forty years of horror arriving all at once
Sister Orla Coyle.voice: Barely speaks; hums; when she does speak it is in a child's sing-song

The Chapel of the Long Wake.name: The Chapel of the Long Wake

plot_local.fact: Thane Hearthless killed Hollow Choir disciple Brother Quell on the Spine Road eleven days ago and harvested his Lagging Shadow power. The Choir has not found the body.
The Choir needs Pip alive and dreaming: each night he dreams in the Quiet Rooms, they map more of the way to Aldrumm's true heart (Choir clock ticks once per day).

BONE-QUAKE (Stirring 4): Rib Row tilted several degrees; sealed Marrow Pit Number Nine collapsed, opening a shaft down toward the heart-cavity. The Hollow Choir now knows exactly where the true heart is: behind a door set in the bone with a lock shaped like an open hand.
Aldrumm felt his grandson die inside his own dream. Three hundred years asleep, and the first thing he has woken enough to feel is grief.

CHOIR CLOCK FULL (dawn, 5th of Harvestwane): the Hollow Choir went down the collapsed shaft of Pit Nine to the heart's door and pressed Thane's dead Hearthblood hand to the lock. The door opened a crack. The Carrion Queen has begun to feed. Across Godbones every marrow lamp is dimming and the bones have begun, very slowly, to grey.

Vane, exposed and burned, moved the Heartstone out of the Chapel reliquary (where to is not yet known) and sent a note to Gristle's shop by a Hollow-sung runner: 'The lamp for the acolyte. Midnight. The Chapel steps. Come alone, little hearth.'

Wenna Tull says at least twelve more Guild children are still Hollow-sung in the Chapel's Quiet Rooms. Brannoc Tull says the Chapel was built by Guild hands three hundred years ago: there is an old coal-and-ash chute from the Chapel kitchens down into the upper Marrow Pits that nobody in the Chapel remembers.
The Heartstone is on Deacon Vane's body, strapped under the burn bandages on her arm. She means to carry it through the heart's door to the Carrion Queen herself.

lore.fact: Thane Hearthless carries Aldrumm's blood (Hearthblood). Nobody in Godbones knows yet.
Pip's word is a Marrowtongue hearth-word (kindling / home-fire). Mother Gristle's cheek scar is the same word, burned in when she learned it.

Thane's Lamp: Thane Hearthless's cracked marrow lamp, now kept by Aldrumm's promise. It never goes out (not for wind, water, or the Carrion Queen). Its light is true hearth-light: the Queen's hymn burns out of anyone standing in it, and the Hollow-sung cannot abide it. Every hearth-fire in Godbones now crackles with Thane's name.

The Heartstone in the hand-shaped lock: set with Aldrumm's word (hearth or waking), it SEALS the heart's door forever. Set with the Carrion hymn, sung through to the end (a three-round rite), it opens the door forever and the Queen walks in.

session_events.fact: Deacon Vane, helped by two market porters, is carrying the unconscious Pip up the climb toward the Chapel of the Long Wake. She did not notice Thane's wrist.

Thane spoke Pip's word (a hearth-word of Marrowtongue) untutored in Gristle's doorway, reaching for Aldrumm. Nat 20: Aldrumm answered and paid half the Toll. Gristle's cold stove roared alight and the word-shaped burn scar on her cheek glowed. The Stirring rose to 1.
The Chapel bell stopped. Deacon Vane took Pip into the Chapel's Quiet Rooms. Thane chose to stay and seek a real Marrowtongue apprenticeship from Gristle rather than chase the procession.

Training day two: Thane's first binding-word test misfired (bound his own jaw); he used the Stopping. By evening he was proficient and could bind reliably. At dusk Deacon Ilsabet Vane knocked at the front of Gristle's shop, asking about the stove that relit itself.

Thane reached for Aldrumm a second time to bind Deacon Vane to her oath (cast 18 vs DC 15, success). Calling the god moved the Stirring +2 (now 3/6), crossing 2: tonight the whole town shares a dream of Aldrumm. His blood-oath to Gristle burned him for 6 HP. The Toll came up as Collapse (0 HP); the working is held on his tongue, not yet tied off.

Thane took Gristle's hand to share the Toll: took 18, dropped to 0 HP, failed one death save, and Gristle stabilized him (Medicine 18). Exhaustion 1. The binding HELD: Deacon Vane is compelled to return Pip home, whole and himself, by tomorrow's supper bell. Vane saw Gristle pay half the Toll and now knows Gristle is a Marrowtongue speaker allied with the hidden Hearthblood.

In the shared dream Thane tried to burn Deacon Vane with the hearth-word and invite Aldrumm in (Grand working). Cast 7 vs DC 20: FAILED. The reach still moved the Stirring +2 (now 5/6). His oath burned him for 10 at 0 HP: one death-save failure, no longer stable. The Toll came due in full (death unless shared). Vane saw his face and the vertebrae cord in the dream.

Thane Hearthless, Aldrumm's many-times-grandson, died on a pallet in the back room of Gristle's Pickles & Preserves on the night of the 4th of Harvestwane, Year 302, paying the Toll in full. At the end he let go of Gristle's hand so she would not die with him.

After midnight on the 4th, the Hollow-sung came to Gristle's shop. Gristle held the back door with the binding-word (14 vs 15, failed by one): they broke through the front, took Thane's body, and left Gristle unconscious and badly hurt among the broken jars. She lives.

Answer to Pip's prayer: the grey patch of dying bone by his bed went soft and warm along an old marrow-vein seam. Pip scraped through with his knife (Stealth 17 vs 13), unheard by the Hollow-sung acolyte outside, and dropped into a warm marrow vein leading down toward the heart.

Pip kept his vow at the heart-cavity: Aldrumm woke THROUGH him (cast 20 vs DC 20). The god shared the Toll; Pip collapsed to 0 HP, went 1 success / 1 failure on death saves, and was stabilized by a freed acolyte. THE STIRRING HIT 6: Aldrumm opened one eye. His hearth-fire burned the Carrion Queen's hymn out of the four Hollow-sung (now ordinary, dazed acolytes again). The god pulled Thane's dead hand from the lock and the heart's door slammed shut on the Queen. The grey-robed Choir cantor fled through the crack before it closed. Across Godbones every marrow lamp flared gold and the greying of the bones stopped. The Skull, a day north, unsealed.

Pip stayed hidden in the heart-cavity all day so Vane could not keep her oath, and short-rested (8/15 HP). He sent Acolyte Benedek up to the Chapel to find the Heartstone. Benedek (nat 1) was caught by Deacon Vane within the hour; terrified, he told her Pip was in the heart-cavity with a lamp that would not go out. Vane went for Pit Nine to fetch Pip (search 9 vs 18, failed): the shaft's lip was crowded with Brannoc Tull's Guild crews digging out the quake-trapped, and the hearth-light rising from below would not let her descend.

SUPPER BELL, 5th of Harvestwane: Vane's bound oath broke. The binding Thane tied with Aldrumm's own hand burned her: hearth-fire ran out of her wrist and set her late shadow alight, and the Carrion hymn screamed out of her mouth in front of Brannoc Tull and forty Guild scrapers at the mouth of Pit Nine. Her cover is gone. Badly burned, she fled toward the Chapel.

Evening of the 5th: Pip led three freed acolytes carrying Thane's body up the collapsed shaft of Pit Nine by Thane's Lamp. Wenna Tull slipped and broke her leg (carry check failed); Guild ropes caught her and the body. Brannoc Tull, seeing his missing niece come up out of the god's heart by hearth-light, was warm to Pip (reaction 11) and sent six scrapers with him and Thane's body to Gristle's shop.

Before midnight Gristle taught Pip the Stopping (19 vs 12). At midnight: Gristle went alone to the Chapel steps and kept Deacon Vane talking (Deception 14 vs Insight 11; Vane believes Pip is coming). Twenty Guild men under Brannoc went quiet into the upper pits for the old ash-chute. Pip went up the marrow vein into his old cell (Stealth 24), found Benedek, and held Thane's Lamp to the door grille: the Hollow-sung guard's hymn burned out of him and, weeping and confused, he unlocked the door.

Fight in the Quiet Rooms ward: Pip rigged a drying-line snare (nat 20). His hearth-word at Coyle's grey lamp failed (11 vs 13); he used the Stopping (dull ache, no Toll). Sister Coyle charged at the sound, hit the line at the throat (14 vs 25), went down prone and lost her tuning fork. Thane's Lamp burned her (4) but she resisted blinding (15 vs 12). Pip cut her throat (17 vs AC 12, 6 dmg): wounded, not dead, voice ruined. Her rasped hymn-note failed on him (save 18). Coyle 12/22. The children's humming is faltering without the fork.

Round 2: Pip clubbed Sister Coyle across the head with Thane's Lamp (15 vs AC 12; 2 bludgeoning + 2 hearth-burn). The lamp's glow burned her again (6). She clawed Pip's face (14 vs AC 13, 3 dmg). Coyle is at 2/22, barely conscious, the hymn guttering in her. Pip 5/15. The Guild broke through the kitchen ash-chute wall at the end of the round.

Pip held Thane's Lamp over the dying Sister Coyle (roll 20): the hymn burned out of her and Orla Coyle of Fourth Pit, gone forty years, came back as herself at 1 HP. Pip raised the lamp over the ward and all fourteen Guild children woke from the hymn. The Guild carried them out through the ash-chute. Orla whispered: Vane has the Heartstone strapped under the bandages on her burned arm.

When the Guild brought down the ward wall, Vane knew she'd been played. She struck Mother Gristle down on the Chapel steps with the Carrion hymn (Gristle alive, unconscious, Mallow with her) and ran for Pit Nine with the Heartstone, now that the Guild has left the shaft and Thane's Lamp is no longer below.

The race to the heart's door: Vane, one-armed and burned, got down Pit Nine (12) before Pip came out of the marrow vein (7; stuck at the fat bit). When Pip arrived she had already pressed the Heartstone into the hand-shaped lock and begun the three-round Carrion rite to open the door forever (one round sung). The Guild is about three rounds behind.

At the heart's door: Pip held Thane's Lamp on Vane. Round 2 she burned (6) but held the hymn (19): rite at 2/3. Round 3 Pip ran in to tear the Heartstone out of the lock (7 vs 13, failed: the half-sung lock gripped it and seared his palm, 1 dmg). Then, at point-blank in the lamp's glow, the hearth-light burned Vane for 11 and she fell at 0 HP before the third verse. The rite is broken. The Heartstone is still in the lock, flickering red and grey. Vane is down and dying. The Guild is one round away.

player_choices.fact: Thane swore on his Hearthblood to Mother Gristle that when he wakes Aldrumm, he will wake him slow, so the god does not roll over the town. In return she teaches him Marrowtongue.
Pip prayed to Aldrumm for all the hearths of Godbones, asked him for guidance, and offered himself to wake the god when he reaches the heart.
Pip spent the god's promise on Thane: 'Keep the lamp man. Give him his grandson, who died to get me out.' Aldrumm kept it.

plot_world.fact: Aldrumm the Hearthfather is awake, or one eye of him is: a vast amber light now burns in the eye-socket of the Skull, visible from every street in Godbones. He has not moved. Nobody knows what he wants yet.

Aldrumm cannot wake further than one eye without moving, and if he moves, Godbones dies. He asks that the Heartstone (held by the Chapel of the Long Wake) be brought to his heart's door: set in the hand-shaped lock, it will seal the door against the Carrion Queen forever.

The Last Heartbeat.description: Bring the Heartstone from the Chapel of the Long Wake down to the door of Aldrumm's heart and set it in the hand-shaped lock to seal the Carrion Queen out forever, before she forces the door.
locations: The Chapel of the Long Wake

events.event: Thread seeded

active.trigger: Thane deliberately pushes The Stirring up by 2 or more at once

active.consequence: [Clock — The Stirring] Aldrumm opens one eye. The Skull unseals. Everything changes. (Thresholds: 2 shared dreams, 4 bone-quake.)

resolved.trigger: Deacon Ilsabet Vane gets a clear look at Thane's left wrist

resolved.consequence: The Hollow Choir sends the Hollow-sung for Mother Gristle at her shop: polite, tireless, at the door after midnight.
resolved.trigger: the night after Vane reports to the Choir (the next time a night passes with Gristle at her shop)

resolved.consequence: The Hollow Choir comes for Thane's body: the lock on the heart's door is shaped like an open hand, and a Hearthblood hand, even a dead one, might fit it.
resolved.trigger: the Choir moves on the heart's door, or anyone goes looking for Thane's body

resolved.consequence: [Clock — The Hollow Choir claims Aldrumm's heart] The Choir finds the true heart through stolen dreams and the Heartstone, and the Carrion Queen begins to finish her meal. The Stirring jumps to 4, and the Ribcage starts to die for good.
resolved.trigger: the The Hollow Choir claims Aldrumm's heart clock ran out

resolved.consequence: Aldrumm, god of kept promises, holds Pip to his offer: at the heart, the god will try to wake THROUGH Pip. Waking him that way will push the Stirring to 6 and cost Pip dearly (the Toll of a god's waking, unless shared).
resolved.trigger: Pip reaches Aldrumm's heart or the door with the hand-shaped lock

resolved.consequence: Vane, exposed and burned, moves the Heartstone out of the Chapel reliquary to keep it from the little hearth, or tries to use Benedek to bargain for Thane's Lamp.
resolved.trigger: the next time anyone goes looking for the Heartstone, or Pip leaves the heart-cavity

ladder.cost: A clean working. A dull ache behind the eyes, nothing more.
Winded and shaking: 1 level of exhaustion until a short rest.
The body pays in blood: lose 1d8 HP per spell tier and gain 1 level of exhaustion.
Collapse: drop to 0 HP and begin dying. The working still completes.
The bill comes due in full: the caster dies unless someone shares the cost (an ally can pay half).

thresholds.consequence: Shared dreams: the whole town dreams the same dream of Aldrumm that night; the Chapel announces a miracle and raises the dream-blessing fee.
Bone-quake: the Ribcage shifts. Rib Row tilts, a Marrow Pit collapses, and the Hollow Choir learns exactly where the heart is.
Aldrumm opens one eye. The Skull unseals. Everything changes.

tiers.reaction: Hostile: calls the watch, slams the door, or worse.
Cold: civil but unhelpful, wants payment or proof first.
Neutral: will deal fairly, will not take risks for you.
Warm: offers help, gossip, or a discount.
Devoted: treats you as kin of the Bearing; will take real risks for you.

thresholds.consequence: Cravings: raw marrow and carrion smell like supper. WIS save DC 12 to refuse when it is offered or near.
The rot shows (grey veins, a sweet-sick smell, a shadow that lags). Disadvantage on Bearer Standing rolls with anyone who notices, and any Hollow Choir member within a street can sense you.
Hollow-sung: the Carrion Queen's hymn fills the empty places. The character is lost to her and becomes an NPC of the Choir (run the Death Protocol hand-off).

world-bible.json.name: Godbones

voice.style: Pratchett-style: warm, dry, omniscient narrator who knows exactly how absurd everyone is and likes them anyway. Long sentences that wander and then land a punchline in the last four words. Grand mythic statements immediately undercut by small domestic detail. Wry asides that state the obvious nobody wanted said. Plain, concrete diction, no purple prose. Humor carries the darkness instead of hiding it.
sample_passages: Three hundred years ago the god Aldrumm fell out of the sky, which is the sort of thing that happens to gods eventually, and landed across the Weeping Valley like a dropped coat. The people of the valley did what people always do with a disaster: they waited a respectful week, then moved in.
The Chapel of the Long Wake held that Aldrumm was merely sleeping. This was a comfort to the faithful and a considerable relief to the Chapel's accountants, since nobody tithes to a corpse.

Magic, old Mother Gristle told her apprentices, is very simple. You say the true name of a thing in the god's own tongue, and the thing listens. Then it sends you the bill. Most people who die of magic, she added, die of not reading the bill.

world-bible.json.tone: Dark with humor. Death, debt, and divine murder are real and lethal; the people living through them are petty, funny, stubborn, and kind at inconvenient moments.
themes: living off the dead: a whole town that eats, burns, and sells pieces of its god
inheritance and lineage: who gets to own a god's body, and who did the actual hauling
faith as a business: the Chapel needs Aldrumm asleep, not dead and not awake
the price of power: every word of magic is paid for in the caster's own body
an unfinished murder: the goddess who killed Aldrumm has not stopped working

snapshot.rules.md:
# Godbones: House Rules

Core: d20 + stat mod (+ proficiency where it fits) vs DC (10 easy, 15 moderate, 20 hard, 25 brutal). D&D-style HP, AC, death saves.

## Marrowtongue (magic)
- Speak the true name of a thing in the dead god's tongue and it obeys. Any effect is possible; the cost scales with ambition.
- **Know the word first.** Casting needs the right words. Words come from a Lantern Tutor (safe, slow, expensive) or from guessing (INT or WIS check, DC by how obscure the word is; on a fail the word means something else).
- **Casting check:** INT (studied) or WIS (instinctive) vs DC set by the effect's scale.
- **Spell tier (severity for the Toll):**
  - 0 Cantrip-scale: light a wick, warm your hands, find a dropped key.
  - 2 Minor: shove a person, mend a bone-crack, silence a room.
  - 5 Major: hurl someone across a street, heal a mortal wound, put out a house fire.
  - 9 Grand: bend a rib, still a crowd, speak to the dead god.
  - 14 Mythic: anything a god would hesitate over.
- **Untutored:** +3 severity until a Tutor has taught you at least the basics of the word.
- **Near the bones:** a Major-or-larger working inside the Ribcage advances The Stirring by 1 (Grand or larger by 2).
- **The Toll:** after the working, roll the Toll (price roll) with severity = tier (+3 if untutored). Read the ladder. An ally who knows even one word can take half the cost.

## The Stirring (0-6)
Town-wide meter of how close Aldrumm is to waking. Rises from big magic near the bones, desecration, and Choir rites. Thresholds: 2 shared dreams, 4 bone-quake, 6 an eye opens.

## Bearer Standing
Opening reaction of townsfolk: 2d6 + standing (-3 to +3). Bearer's Ring or a known kindness to the old families raises it; a known slight lowers it.

## Marrow
Common currency of the trade alongside coin. A thumb-vial of raw marrow sells for about 5 sp; refined lamp-marrow about 2 gp.

## Carrion Rot (0-6, PC vital `rot`)
Stolen Choir power rots the thief.
- **Harvest:** when you kill a Choir disciple you may eat their last breath to take one of their powers. +1 Rot, and a CON save DC 13 or +1 more.
- **Using a stolen power:** +1 Rot per use unless the power says otherwise.
- **Thresholds:** 2 cravings · 4 visible rot, Choir can sense you within a street · 6 Hollow-sung (character lost).
- **Lowering Rot:** not yet known. Rumor says the Chapel, the Tutors, and the Hearthfather himself each have an answer, and each answer costs something.
snapshot.session-log.md:
# Session Log - Godbones

*A new adventure begins...*

---

## World Summary
Three hundred years ago the god Aldrumm the Hearthfather was killed by the Carrion Queen and fell across the Weeping Valley. Twelve Bearer families dragged the body into place and built the town of Godbones inside the ribcage. The Chapel of the Long Wake insists he is only sleeping. Marrow yields are dropping, the town shares dreams, and the Hollow Choir has arrived.

- **Starting location:** Rib Row, market lane along the seventh rib. Midday, market day, 3rd of Harvestwane, Year 302 of the Bearing.
- **On stage:** Mother Gristle (Lantern Tutor, pickle shop), Pip Haddersley (street kid speaking Marrowtongue in his sleep), Deacon Ilsabet Vane (Chapel, secretly Hollow Choir).
- **Hook:** Pip collapses mid-street and speaks a word of the god's tongue; lamps flare, a window shatters. Vane wants to carry him to the Chapel "for care." Gristle has gone very still.
- **Threat clock:** The Hollow Choir claims Aldrumm's heart (0/4).

---

character.background: Rib Row street kid and part-time marrow-thief

features: Natural Speaker: dreams words of Marrowtongue untaught. Knows the hearth-word (UNTUTORED: +3 Toll severity). Casts with WIS (+2), no proficiency yet.
Dream-map: knows the way through the god's body to the door with the hand-shaped lock, from a month of drawing it. Can find it awake, in the dark, by feel.
Small and Quick: fits through gaps adults cannot; advantage on Stealth in crowds and on Rib Row.
Gutter Knowledge: knows every alley, drain, rooftop, and fence on Rib Row, and who will buy stolen marrow.

The waking-word (rise / stand / open your eyes), UNTUTORED: spoken once, at the heart, to wake Aldrumm. Rouse the sleeping, steady the dying, shake off a spell. Near the bones it can move the Stirring.
Woke the God: Aldrumm knows Pip by name. (His promise to Pip is SPENT: he kept Thane.)
The Stopping (taught by Mother Gristle): once per working, abort a spell before the Toll lands; pay only the first rung (a dull ache) and the spell fails.
character.notes: Saw the lamp man (Thane) die in the shared dream on the night of the 4th. Deacon Vane is magically bound to have him home, whole and himself, by supper on the 5th.
